narrative.overview:
The personal archive puts typography in the foreground. Heavy condensed sans-serif
and upright serif forms give ordinary titles distinct compositions; quiet body
copy and metadata keep the reading path clear. Warm charcoal and paper sections
provide a stable structure beneath the changes in scale and alignment.

This is the approved production system for the homepage and shared index.
Its character comes from type, whitespace, controlled asymmetry, and real content.
Individual pages will own their visual systems, developed with the owner section
by section. The first custom pages and listing previews were rejected and removed;
their reserved folders are empty. The homepage's specific composition is recorded
in its surface brief.

Personality comes from the material Tristan publishes, rather than a fictional
newspaper, museum, scrapbook, or permanent subject theme. Trips, passing thoughts,
writing, and code share this visual identity without needing identical treatments.
The scale contrast and independent experiences of henry.codes inform the direction;
the compositions and personal details remain Tristan's own.

Annotations, footnotes, pixel art, diagrams, and small interactions may add
character when the content earns them. They are optional contributions, not
required decorations or a reason to fill every quiet space. The approved homepage
continues to use its typographic identity without a pixel logo.
keyCharacteristics: Dramatic scale contrast between condensed sans-serif and upright serif type.
Warm charcoal and paper surfaces with monochrome resting states.
Fluid gutters, full available width, and deliberate changes in alignment.
Flat, square geometry with rules that mark meaningful boundaries.
Restrained interaction and visible content before JavaScript.

rules.name: The Resting Monochrome Rule
rules.body: Keep the homepage and index monochrome. Published entry links respond with underlines on hover and keyboard focus, within the existing charcoal and paper palette.

rules.name: The Upright Serif Rule
rules.body: Keep Marcellus upright in the shared identity and homepage emphasis; semantic emphasis does not introduce an italic display style.

dos: Do use charcoal and paper for shared page surfaces and adapt muted text to its surface.
Do pair heavy Barlow Condensed with upright Marcellus in the shared identity; keep its Mrs Saint Delafield signature on the homepage middle name.
Do preserve fluid gutters, available width, clear boundaries, and controlled asymmetry.
Do keep entries and metadata readable before JavaScript and without hover.
Do preserve keyboard focus, touch targets, reduced-motion paths, and static content before JavaScript.
Do preserve optional content fields and develop each page's visual system with the owner section by section.
Do keep planned entries as plain text until their destination pages exist.
Do call catalog records entries and their destinations pages.
donts: Don't restore the red accent, Inter display system, or global theme toggle to the shared shell.
Don't add a top homepage navbar, pixel logo, or artificial maximum page width.
Don't turn entries into identical cards or tags into pills.
Don't add decorative shadows or borders around every region.
Don't introduce another resting page-surface color or persistent chromatic color on the homepage or index.
Don't treat the signature overlap as a general layout device or impose the shared layout on independent pages.
Don't restore the rejected page or preview treatments or require a shared MDX visual template.
Don't tie the archive to a permanent subject theme or add decorative oddities to fill space.
